channel.title: Daily Signal — The Great Repurpose
channel.description: A daily five-story briefing reading AI news through The Great Repurpose lens.

item.title: Entry-Level Jobs Get Senior AI Standards
item.description: The signal is no longer that AI might someday change work. The signal is that companies are already using it to redraw roles, expectations, and leverage. The human task is to stop treating identity as a job title and start naming the value that travels with you.

item.title: Agents Enter The Real Economy
item.description: AI is moving from answer machine to active participant. That makes the old productivity frame too small. The question becomes who directs the work, what judgment remains human, and where people learn to create with systems instead of merely using tools.

item.title: AI Lays Off America While Apple Launches Siri
item.description: AI is no longer the future of work — it's the present reason people are losing it. But the people who thrive will be those who treat AI as a collaborator, not a replacement. The Great Repurpose isn't a luxury anymore; it's a survival skill.

item.title: AI Reshapes Work, Identity, And Creativity
item.description: The signal is that AI is no longer only changing what people do. It is changing how people understand themselves, how companies explain job cuts, and where creative value lives. The human move is to name the part of us that remains durable before the market names us obsolete.

item.title: Creative Control In The Age Of AI
item.description: The old guard of creative ownership is fighting back. Adobe's Creator Act, the creator economy conversation, and the rise of AI agents all point to the same inflection point: human creators are demanding legal, technical, and economic guardrails over their work. The Great Repurpose is not just about adapting to AI. It is about asserting who owns the output and who gets to decide.

item.title: Creativity Moves Upstream
item.description: The signal is that creativity is becoming more valuable, not less, but it is changing location. As AI absorbs more execution, human advantage moves upstream into taste, judgment, problem selection, and the courage to make something that actually matters.
